explanation: The K101P mutation eliminates a positively charged lysine that makes favorable electrostatic or polar interactions with nevirapine at the pocket rim (minimum distance 2.7 Å), replacing it with the conformationally restricted proline whose neutral character and reduced volume cannot maintain these contacts. The loss of the charged side chain removes a stabilizing interaction network while the conformational constraint imposed by proline's cyclic structure likely disrupts the local geometry needed for optimal ligand positioning in the NNRTI-binding pocket. Together, these factors—elimination of electrostatic stabilization and geometric remodeling of the binding interface—incrementally destabilize nevirapine binding despite the modest thermodynamic penalty, allowing viral escape.
